rule: Accept phone numbers in flexible formats with spaces, hyphens, dashes, brackets, and country codes.
quote: Let users enter phone numbers in whatever format is familiar to them. Allow for additional spaces, hyphens, dashes and brackets, and be able to accommodate country and area codes.

rule: Provide inline change links alongside each answer so users can edit without leaving the page.
quote: < a class = "govuk-link" href = "#" > Change < span class = "govuk-visually-hidden" > name </ span > </ a >

rule: Use visually hidden text to clarify what each change link modifies for screen reader users.
quote: < span class = "govuk-visually-hidden" > name </ span >

rule: Help users understand the order tasks must be completed in and which ones are done.
quote: Help users understand: the tasks involved in completing a transaction the order they should complete tasks in when they've completed tasks

rule: Only use a task list page for longer transactions spanning multiple sessions.
quote: Only use a complete multiple tasks page for longer transactions involving multiple tasks that users may need to complete over a number of sessions.

rule: Show a reference number prominently so users can track their application.
quote: Your reference number < br > < strong > HDJ2123F </ strong >

rule: Explain what happens next and when so users know what to expect after submission.
quote: Your confirmation page must include: a reference number, if there is one details of what happens next and when

rule: Allow users to save or bookmark confirmation pages as receipts.
quote: Some users will bookmark the confirmation page as a form of receipt. You should allow them to return to the page, whenever possible.

rule: Include links to information users are likely to need next after completing a transaction.
quote: links to information or services that users are likely to need next

rule: Ask only one question per page to help users focus and understand what is being asked.
quote: Start by asking one question per page Asking just one question per question page helps users understand what you're asking them to do

rule: Include a back link at the top of question pages so users can change previous answers without trusting the browser back button.
quote: Some users do not trust browser back buttons when they're entering data. Always include a Back link component at the top of question pages

rule: Never mark mandatory fields with asterisks; use (optional) for optional fields instead.
quote: Never mark mandatory fields with asterisks.

rule: Pre-populate fields or show carried-forward responses to avoid asking users to re-enter known information.
quote: If the same type of information is needed more than once, make it easier to reuse previously entered answers through one of these methods: pre-populating the relevant fields showing carried-forward responses

rule: Make the reason for asking each question clear to users.
quote: On every question page you should: make sure it's clear to users why you're asking each question

rule: Use action-focused button text like Start now or Sign in rather than generic labels.
quote: include a 'button' linking into the service, with text that's consistent with the action you're asking users to take – for example, 'Start now', 'Sign in'

rule: List documents and information users will need before starting the service.
quote: You'll also need to list any documents or information the user will need to help them complete the service

rule: Ask eligibility questions inside the service rather than blocking users at the start page.
quote: Avoid using the start point to provide complex eligibility information. Instead, ask questions inside the service to find out whether the user is eligible.

rule: Use interruption pages sparingly and only when users might make a costly or irreversible mistake.
quote: Use Interruption pages to warn the user before they: do something unusual that's probably a mistake do something that cannot be undone

rule: Keep interruption panel content short and do not include form elements inside the panel.
quote: Keep information within the panel short. Do not place any other components or form elements inside the panel.

rule: Only use interruption pages when there is clear evidence of need and no other way to prevent the error.
quote: Do not use Interruption pages unless you're confident that both: there's evidence of a clear need to pause the user journey it's the only way to give the user information

rule: Document and share research findings with team members, managers, and the public when appropriate.
quote: Share your findings. Document and share your research findings with team members, managers, and the public whenever practical.

rule: Use straightforward plain language on 404 pages; structure includes heading, explanation, fixes, actions, and support channels.
quote: This kind of error can be frustrating or confusing. Straightforward plain language can help. Use a 404 page to explain the error and instruct the user what to do next.

rule: Provide context explaining why account creation is needed; remove unnecessary distractions from the page.
quote: The best way to help is to provide context about why they're creating an account and to remove unnecessary distractions from the page.

rule: Use a shared authentication service where possible to ensure consistency across government websites.
quote: You should use a shared service or the authentication page templates to create a more consistent experience across sites and services.

rule: Display form controls in HTML order matching screen order; do not use CSS to rearrange them.
quote: Display form controls in the same order in the HTML as they appear on screen. Don't use CSS to rearrange the form controls.

rule: Align validation messages visually with their input fields for screen magnifier users.
quote: Visually align validation messages with the input fields so people using screen magnifiers can read them quickly.

rule: Group related form controls in fieldset elements with legend labels for screen reader users.
quote: Group each set of thematically related controls in a fieldset element. Use the legend element to offer a label within each one.

rule: Use simple vertical layouts for forms to aid users with limited vision who scan left-to-right.
quote: Keep your form blocks in a vertical pattern. This approach is ideal, from an accessibility standpoint, because of limited vision that makes it hard to scan from right to left.

rule: Avoid disabled form states; use helper text, tooltips and inline validation instead.
quote: Avoid disabled states, especially for text inputs. Disabled states have low color contrast, do not offer meaningful feedback to screen reader users, and keyboard navigators can't focus on them.

rule: Use aria-disabled and JavaScript to disable elements when necessary, not the disabled HTML attribute.
quote: Support screen reader users and keyboard navigators by using aria-disabled=true instead of the disabled attribute to indicate the presence of a disabled element

rule: Add the required HTML attribute to form inputs to enforce field validation before submission.
quote: Add the required attribute to your form elements to indicate that a field must be filled out before submitting the form.

rule: Label optional fields with the word optional in parentheses.
quote: Mark optional fields as "optional." Label optional fields with the word "optional" placed in parentheses.

rule: Align primary action buttons to the left edge of forms.
quote: Align the primary action button to the left edge of your form.

rule: Make buttons stretch full width on mobile for easier pressing with one hand.
quote: On smaller screens, such as on mobile, buttons stretch across the screen's width. This makes them easier to press for users holding a phone in their right hand.

rule: Use only one primary button per page to avoid reducing its impact and user clarity.
quote: Use only 1 primary button on a page. Having more than 1 reduces their impact and makes it harder for users to know what to do next.

rule: Ensure button contrast ratio of at least 3:1 with dark backgrounds to meet WCAG 2.2 AA.
quote: The background colour must have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 with white to meet WCAG 2.2 success criterion 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast, level AA

rule: Use cards to visually group related content and actions so users complete tasks more quickly.
quote: Use a card to visually group related content and actions to help users do what they need to more quickly.

rule: Avoid wrapping entire clickable cards in anchor tags due to poor screen reader experience.
quote: For clickable cards, avoid wrapping the entire card in an anchor tag as this can be a difficult experience for screen reader users.

rule: Keep card content short so users can scan for relevant and actionable information quickly.
quote: Keep the card short so it is easy to scan for relevant and actionable information.

rule: Use checkboxes to let users select one or more options from a set on a form.
quote: Use checkboxes to let users select 1 or more options on a form.

rule: Use date input to help users enter dates like appointment dates with separate day, month, year fields.
quote: Use date input to help users enter a date, like an appointment date.

rule: Use details component to let users reveal information only when needed, making pages easier to scan.
quote: Make a page easier to scan by letting users reveal more detailed information only if they need it.

rule: Make details link text short and descriptive so users quickly decide if they need to click.
quote: Make the link text short and descriptive so users can quickly work out if they need to click on it.

rule: Avoid using details in transactional forms; users may mistake blue text for a navigation link.
quote: users being reluctant to expand the details component in user testing sessions for transactional services (forms). When asked why they wouldn't click, they explained that they thought the link text (blue underlined text) would take them to a new page

rule: Explain what went wrong and how to fix it in every error message.
quote: Explain what went wrong and how to fix it.

rule: Use red borders to visually connect error messages to their corresponding form fields.
quote: use a red border to visually connect the message and the question it belongs to

rule: Always show an error summary at the top of the page, even if only one mistake exists.
quote: Always show an error summary when there is a validation error, even if there's only 1 mistake.

rule: Move keyboard focus to the error summary when the page loads so screen readers announce it immediately.
quote: move the keyboard focus to the error summary

rule: Link each error in the summary to the corresponding form field for easy navigation.
quote: link to each of the answers that have validation errors

rule: Do not use expanders on pages with other interactive elements like buttons or text inputs to avoid distraction.
quote: on pages with other interactive elements, such as buttons or text input – there's a risk that expanders will distract users

rule: Place the legend as the first element in a fieldset to describe the group of inputs.
quote: The 1st element in a fieldset must be a <legend> which describes the group of inputs.

rule: Support drag-and-drop file uploads alongside the traditional file picker button.
quote: or drop file

rule: Place an organization logo or service name at the top of every page to confirm the user's location.
quote: Use the appropriate header at the top of every page to show users they are on an NHS service

rule: Include a search function in the header to help users find content quickly.
quote: help them get started in finding what they need

rule: Show the current page and surround it with adjacent page numbers to help users understand their position.
quote: Use pagination to help users navigate forwards and backwards through a series of pages

rule: Use radio buttons when users must select exactly one option from a mutually exclusive list.
quote: Use radios when you want users to select only 1 option from a list

rule: Use select dropdowns only as a last resort for long option lists; prefer radios or checkboxes when possible.
quote: Use select to let users choose an option from a long list but only use it as a last resort

rule: Display a summary list at the end of a form to let users review and edit their responses before submission.
quote: Use the summary list to summarise information, for example, a user's responses at the end of a form

rule: Consider alternatives to tables (summaries, lists, expanders, tabs) for complex data to reduce cognitive overload.
quote: In staff services, complex data tables can lead to cognitive overload, a poor user experience and performance issues

rule: Avoid using tables to lay out page content; use a grid system instead.
quote: Do not use a table to lay out content on a page. Use the grid system instead

rule: Use adjectives rather than verbs for tag labels to avoid users thinking they are clickable.
quote: Use adjectives rather than verbs for the names of your tags. Using a verb might make a user think that clicking on them will do something.

rule: Limit tag statuses to the minimum needed; add more only if user research confirms necessity.
quote: The more you add, the harder it is for users to remember them. So start with the smallest number of statuses you think might work, then add more if your user research shows there's a need for them.

rule: Display task completion status and hints alongside task names to help users identify what they have done and still need to do.
quote: The task list component displays all the tasks a user needs to do, and allows users to easily identify which ones are done and which they still need to do.
